title: Understanding Islam through Hadis
byline: by Ram Swarup · Exposition Press, New York, 1982 · Voice of India reprints 1983 and 1987 · subtitled Religious Faith or Fanaticism?
lede: Ram Swarup reads the Sahih Muslim, one of the two most authoritative Sunni collections of the Prophet's sayings and deeds, in Abdul Hamid Siddiqi's four-volume English translation (Lahore, 1973–75). He follows its own order, from faith and prayer to marriage, crime, war and government. Because Muslim theology treats the Hadis as revelation “made concrete in the life of the Prophet”, he argues it shows Islam as believers are meant to live it. In his reading that Islam is a complete system, political and military as well as devotional. The book is known in India mainly for being banned.

note: This is a critical, outsider's reading of a sacred text. Muslim scholars read the same collection through centuries of commentary and context. The ban on the book is recorded in Freedom of Expression. This page lists what the book covers and summarises the author's stance, attributed to him.
